human_tolerance.notes: The Japanese article records it in suburban gardens and towns as well as woodland, using natural holes, badger and fox dens and even straw piles and abandoned buildings; it is nocturnal but becomes diurnal where people do not disturb it.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: Mating is synchronised between February and April, with a nine-week gestation.

phases.name: young
phases.note: A litter of four to six pups is raised in a den for about two months.

vocalizations.description: A soft growl or groan, the species' main social vocalisation; the article compares its pitch to a domestic cat's.
A high whine exchanged between a pair as they move together at night.
A short, sharp bark given when alarmed; the species also feigns death (thanatosis) when caught.

taxonomy.note: GBIF treats the Japanese raccoon dog as the accepted subspecies Nyctereutes procyonoides viverrinus (usageKey 6164330, authorship Temminck, 1838), while the record follows iNaturalist and recent authorities in treating it as the species Nyctereutes viverrinus, endemic to Japan. Family Canidae, order Carnivora, genus Nyctereutes.

external.note: gbif_usage_key 6164330 is the GBIF key for the subspecies N. p. viverrinus; inat_taxon_id 855310 from the iNaturalist taxa API (active, rank species, preferred common name 'Japanese Raccoon Dog'); wikidata Q122835073 from the English Wikipedia page's wikibase item. The GBIF key and the iNaturalist id name the same animal at different ranks, which the article notes is a matter of ongoing taxonomic debate.

range.note: The English article states the species is endemic to Japan (JP).

traits.note: The Japanese article gives head-body 50-68 cm, tail 12.5-25 cm and mass 4-6 kg (rising to 6-10 kg in autumn); length_m 0.78 is the midpoint of head-body plus tail, and mass 5.0 kg is the midpoint of 4-6 kg. Locomotion Walk, Trot and Climb: the English article says the species climbs trees for fruit using curved claws. Diet is from the Japanese article's omnivorous account (rodents, birds and eggs, amphibians, fish, insects, myriapods, crustaceans, molluscs, carrion and plant material including fruit and nuts), aligned with the EltonTraits MamFuncDat row for the congener Nyctereutes procyonoides (invertebrate 20, vertebrate 40, fruit 30, seed 10). Lifespan 7.5 years is the midpoint of the English article's 7-8 years in the wild. Shoulder height is not given by any source; 0.25 m is a judgement for this famously short-legged canid, whose leg length the article contrasts with the longer-legged mainland raccoon dog.

habitat.note: The Japanese article records it in woodland and suburban gardens, sheltering in natural holes and other animals' dens and sometimes buildings, and climbing for fruit; use ground 0.8 / arboreal 0.2, shelter a burrow, and resources follow the omnivorous diet plus water. human_tolerance is Adapter from its presence in towns and gardens.

seasonal.note: The English article records mating synchronised between February and April, a nine-week gestation, a litter of four to six and about two months of parental care; the breeding and young phases follow that. The Japanese article notes no hibernation in warm regions, so strategy ActiveYearRound.

vocalizations.note: The English article says the species 'vocalizes by growling or with groans that have pitches resembling those of the domesticated cat' and notes it feigns death as a defence. The growl, whine and alarm bark are a judgement mapping that onto three call slots.

look.note: The article describes a stocky canid with short legs and a dark facial mask, and the Japanese article describes a grizzled grey-brown coat; the modelled mask, dark legs and ears, pale snout and dark tail tip follow that. Proportions and palette are judgement, based on the congener red fox record with a shorter, stockier body.

behavior.note: Authored parameters for the shared ground-forager program: the default rest window (sun between 10 and 90 degrees) puts the animal in shelter by day and out at night, matching its nocturnal habit; food_tag invertebrate, walk foraging and a trot escape follow the article's account, and flee_m 30 reflects a wary animal that lives close to people.
